profile.address: Huurrekuja 10, 04360 Tuusula, Finland (per Hetzner's own corporate site; not independently matched to one specific numbered building on the multi-building campus).
profile.reading:
This record covers one of the buildings in Hetzner's Data Center Park in Tuusula, a municipality north of Helsinki, Finland, at Huurrekuja 10, an address Hetzner's own corporate site lists for its Finnish subsidiary. Hetzner Online, the German hosting and cloud company that owns and operates the site, is headquartered in Gunzenhausen, Bavaria, and was founded in 1997 by Martin Hetzner as a web hosting reseller before building its own infrastructure, opening its first company built data center park in Falkenstein, Germany in 2009 and a second in Nuremberg in 2012.

Hetzner began planning a Finnish location around 2015 and invested in the C-Lion1 submarine fiber cable, a roughly 1,100 kilometer link between Rostock, Germany and Helsinki that became operational in 2016, laying communications groundwork ahead of the Nordic expansion. According to Data Center Dynamics, the Tuusula campus itself, built on a roughly 150,000 square meter site, opened its first building in 2018, and by mid-2022 the company had completed a second building there, with groundwork finished for two further buildings and the next one due in the first quarter of 2023. At that point Hetzner's stated plan called for up to ten buildings on the site, with room to expand toward twenty if demand justified it, and the company's People Operations Manager, Riikka Huhtaniitty, was quoted saying growth accelerated by pandemic era demand had pushed the company to almost double its headcount, with further hiring expected as new buildings there came online.

This registry could not confirm from the sources it considers reliable which specific numbered building on the Tuusula campus corresponds to this particular OpenStreetMap record, so no single building level power or floor area figure is asserted here. A figure describing the campus as a whole at 24 megawatts appears on a commercial data center directory site, but this registry does not treat that site as a reliable source and could not corroborate the number through Hetzner's own materials or trade press, so it is omitted rather than repeated as fact. Any power capacity attached to the Tuusula site as a whole should in any case be read as describing the multi-building park rather than this one building specifically.

Company wide, Hetzner describes itself as one of Europe's larger and more trusted infrastructure providers, running dedicated servers, cloud servers, and colocation from data center parks in Falkenstein and Nuremberg in Germany, Tuusula in Finland, Ashburn, Virginia, opened in 2021, Hillsboro, Oregon, opened in 2022, and Singapore, opened in 2024, with 24 hour customer support staffed by its own data center technicians and hardware sourced through partnerships with AMD, Dell, and Intel. By 2022 the company reported roughly 350,000 servers in operation and more than 400 employees, up from about 200,000 hosted domains running on 20,000 servers back in 2008, and by 2025 it reported operating more than 500,000 server units supporting more than one million simultaneously active cloud instances, alongside launching an EMAS environmental certification effort and holding its first company wide Hetzner Summit event. Hetzner Cloud itself launched in 2018 and reportedly reached 100,000 instances within its first year. Finland's cold climate and largely renewable electricity supply are commonly cited industry reasons for siting a Nordic hosting campus there, since outside air can handle much of the cooling load for large parts of the year, though this registry did not find a Hetzner statement making that specific claim about the Tuusula site, so it is offered here only as general context for the choice of location rather than as a company reported efficiency figure.
profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-06. Prior profile version cited datacentermap.com and Wikipedia (twice) in its sources array, both excluded under current house rules, so the entry was redone. The prior research_note also contained a line claiming "prior 2026-09-02 stale out-of-scope flag superseded, see Nasertic changelog entry seq 928/929" -- this registry could not find or verify any such changelog and treats that line as unverifiable, possibly fabricated by an earlier automated pass, and disregards it. The prior profile also asserted it_capacity_mw of 24 (campus-wide, from a banned aggregator) and facility_codes listing HEL1-DC1 through DC14 (also aggregator-sourced, and admitted in the prior note to be an unmatched guess); both have been removed rather than repeated. Fresh research used a DCD article on the campus buildout (2022, one of very few non-aggregator English sources found) and Hetzner's own corporate "about us" and company-history blog pages. Checked and rejected as citations: datacentermap.com, datacenterhawk.com, baxtel.com, inflect.com, ocolo.io, Wikipedia. Attempted businessfinland.com (a Finnish government trade-promotion site, not on the banned list) but it was blocked by robots.txt on fetch; only its search-result title was seen, so it was not used as a cited source. Could not verify: which numbered building (DC1, DC2, etc.) this OSM way corresponds to, and any building-level or reliably-sourced campus-level MW figure. WebSearch quota was exhausted partway through this session; remaining research relied on WebFetch of already-identified URLs plus general knowledge of Hetzner's public history.
profile.campus_power_note: A commercial directory site attributes 24 MW to the whole multi-building Tuusula campus. This registry could not corroborate that figure via Hetzner's own materials or trade press and does not assert it as fact.
